tasks.short: Examine design references, choose engraving methods and record the approach.

steps.what: Retrieve sketches, blueprints and prior job references
Examine diagrams, samples and workpiece constraints
Decide how the design should be etched, cut or engraved
Write the engraving approach and relevant design annotations

tasks.design: Configure a job-indexed reference view and method-note template in {DOCS}. The engraver examines the real sample and workpiece, chooses the approach and separately records it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding references and repeating job context in method notes takes clerical time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document links and annotation templates can preserve job context.
tasks.still_hard: Material response and visual detail determine whether a proposed method will work.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret the intended appearance and recognise process limitations.
tasks.altitude: Keep the method decision connected to its design references.

reach.learn: Use the same reference version and method constraints.

evidence.claim: A native job view and method-note template could reduce retrieval and repeated documentation; this engraving saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: The method note is part of the examination task and is separately priced from inspecting and deciding.

The engraver produces job identifier, reference version, chosen process, orientation and method caveats in s4; 16 retained hours include writing and checking. Unclear design details stay open for manual clarification.
Use native views and annotations first. No AI process selection, machine programming or external send is proposed.
The record saving concerns repeated context and headings, not a same-system save.
unknowns: Whether method notes already use linked references and templates.
research_questions: What portion of method-note time repeats job context rather than adds new judgement?

already_counted.description: Write and check the method record.

incremental.description: Maintain reference links and the method-note template.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=94, gross=6; upkeep=2 gives central net=4. Existing efficient job records could erase the gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design engraving patterns using native geometry and repeat tools.

steps.what: Read the engraving pattern brief and workpiece dimensions
Design the engraving composition and distinctive pattern elements
Enter pattern dimensions, repeat spacing and orientation
Generate repeated pattern geometry from the entered parameters
Inspect and edit the pattern for appearance and engraving suitability
Save the final engraving pattern and reference version

tasks.design: Use native array, alignment and parametric repeat tools in engraving or vector-design software represented by {OTHER}. The engraver chooses the composition, supplies parameters, inspects generated geometry and retains the final file save without claiming a saving for it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated geometry may be drawn, aligned and adjusted individually.
tasks.enabler_now: Native pattern parameters can generate repeated elements from checked source geometry.
tasks.still_hard: Visual quality and engraving suitability require judgement beyond geometric repetition.
tasks.human_edge: Create a composition that fits the brief and the material.
tasks.altitude: Spend drawing time on distinctive design rather than repeated geometry.

reach.learn: Keep source geometry, dimensions and pattern version identifiable.

evidence.claim: Native geometry arrays and parametric repeats can generate repetitive pattern elements; the proposed engraving saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: This scenario contains repetitive pattern geometry currently drawn or aligned manually. One-off freehand designs may have little gain.

The engraver produces scale, units, bounds, repeat count, spacing, orientation and source-geometry version in s3, with all ten hours of capture and checks counted. Invalid or missing parameters stop generation for manual editing in s5.
OTHER means the existing engraving or vector-design application. Native tools come before bespoke generation or AI.
The final file step retains all its current time and has no self-approval gate; no saving is credited to a same-system save and no machine release is proposed.
unknowns: How much geometry is repeated and whether native pattern tools are already used.
research_questions: Does native repeat generation reduce total drawing time after inspection on representative engraving patterns?

incremental.description: Maintain pattern presets and check generated geometry after software changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 repetitive-geometry scenario: B=100, R=75, gross=25; upkeep=5 gives central net=20. Existing native tool use would reduce the gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine settings, adjust mechanical controls and inspect reproduced designs.

steps.what: Look up machine settings and prior roller or plate setup notes
Determine settings for the specific machine, design and material
Move bars or levers to reproduce designs on rollers or plates
Inspect the reproduced design and adjust unsuitable settings
Write the final machine settings and setup caveats

tasks.design: Configure a machine-and-job setup view and setup-note template in {DOCS}. The engraver determines settings, operates the bars or levers and checks the result; software only simplifies reference retrieval and recording.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prior setup details are hard to retrieve and record consistently.
tasks.enabler_now: Native indexing and reusable setup fields can retain the relevant context.
tasks.still_hard: Mechanical adjustment and material response must be checked on the actual machine.
tasks.human_edge: Notice a poor reproduction and adjust controls appropriately.
tasks.altitude: Keep repeat setup knowledge accessible without automating mechanical judgement.

reach.learn: Record machine, material and reference version with settings.

evidence.claim: Native setup indexing and record fields could save a small amount of clerical preparation; this mechanical engraving saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: Reference lookup and setup writing are separately priced from physical adjustment and inspection.

The engraver produces machine identifier, material, design version, settings and setup caveats in s5; four retained hours include capture. Incomplete or outdated reference settings require manual determination in s2.
Use native document views and notes first. No automatic settings transfer, control movement or safety function is proposed.
The setup record has no self-approval gate and the saving is repeated structure, not the save operation.
unknowns: Whether setup notes already provide efficient retrieval and capture.
research_questions: Does indexing reduce search time without encouraging reuse of unsuitable settings?

already_counted.description: Capture and check the setup note.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 small-clerical scenario: B=100, R=97, gross=3; upkeep=1 gives central net=2. Mechanical work retains all its time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep material, appearance and machine decisions human while simplifying repetitive pattern geometry and records.
reach: Link design references, pattern versions and setup notes.
role.ambitious_version: An engraver who spends more time on distinctive design and reliable execution, with repeat details handled consistently.
